---
title: "Kenya - Maize: is fertiliser worth it?"
nocite: |
  @faostat_qcl, @kiwia2022
subtitle: "Thirty-three long-rains seasons in the western highlands, four nitrogen rates. The model says yes, every year. The useful question is how wrong it can be before the answer changes"
---

```{ojs}
import {withDownload, cellFeatures, fmt, locatorMap, placeMarks, boxPolygon} from "../assets/js/dl.js"
S = FileAttachment("data/kenya/summary.json").json()
B = FileAttachment("data/kenya/boundaries.json").json()
countries = FileAttachment("data/kenya/countries.geojson").json()
adm1 = FileAttachment("data/kenya/adm1.geojson").json()
adm2 = FileAttachment("data/kenya/adm2.geojson").json()
years = FileAttachment("data/kenya/years.csv").csv({typed: true})
price = FileAttachment("data/kenya/maize_price_eldoret.csv").csv({typed: true})
cells = FileAttachment("data/kenya/cells.csv").csv({typed: true})
RATES = [0, 60, 120, 180]
STEPS = [[0, 60], [60, 120], [120, 180]]
stepName = k => `${STEPS[k][0]} to ${STEPS[k][1]} kg N`
MARKET = 1 / (1 - S.moisture)          // dry matter to grain at market moisture
KIWIA_AEN = 21                          // Kenya on-farm trials, kg grain per kg N (Kiwia et al. 2022, Fig. 4a)
byYear = d3.rollups(years, v => Object.fromEntries(v.map(d => [d.n, d.yield])), d => d.season_year)
  .map(([year, y]) => ({year, y})).sort((a, b) => a.year - b.year)
resp = RATES.map(n => {
  const v = years.filter(d => d.n === n).map(d => d.yield)
  return {n, mean: d3.mean(v), p10: d3.quantile(v, 0.1), p50: d3.quantile(v, 0.5), p90: d3.quantile(v, 0.9)}
})
aeModel = d3.mean(byYear, d => (d.y[60] - d.y[0]) / 60)
anchor = KIWIA_AEN / (aeModel * MARKET)
vcrClass = v => v < 1 ? "below 1: loses money" : v < 2 ? "1 to 2: pays back" : v < 4 ? "2 to 4: doubles the money" : "4 or more: safe bet"
vcrColor = ({domain: ["below 1: loses money", "1 to 2: pays back", "2 to 4: doubles the money", "4 or more: safe bet"],
             range: ["#c0392b", "#e0a030", "#7fb3d5", "#1f5f99"]})
```

| Setup | |
|---|---|
| Area | 34.6-35.6 E, 0.1-1.1 N, western Kenya (counties below) |
| Crop map | MapSPAM 2020 maize, physical area [@spam2020] |
| Weather, soil | AgERA5 1990-2024 [@agera5]; SoilGrids 2.0 [@poggio2021], one profile per 0.1° cell |
| Crop, template | CERES-Maize, hybrid H610 (DSSAT cultivar IB0060), template `XDMZ8201.MZX`; the model simulates water and nitrogen (phosphorus, potassium and diseases are off) |
| Treatments | rainfed; 0, 60, 120 or 180 kg N/ha as urea, a third at sowing and two thirds 35 days later |
| Sowing | 15 March every year, the long rains |
| Years | 1991-2023, 33 seasons |
| Prices | maize: WFP monthly wholesale price, Eldoret [@wfp_kenya_prices]; fertiliser: three bag prices reported in 2022 and 2023 [@capitalfm2022; @capitalfm2023] |
| Boundaries | edge-matched OCHA administrative boundaries (COD-AB) from HDX: [Kenya](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-ken) (IEBC), [Uganda](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-uga) (UBOS), CC BY-IGO |
| Experiment file | [`configs/cases/kenya-maize.yml`](https://github.com/bennyistanto/xdssat/blob/main/configs/cases/kenya-maize.yml) |

## Four bags, four harvests

A 50 kg bag of urea holds 23 kg of nitrogen. The question a maize grower asks is simple: does the grain the
bag adds sell for more than the bag costs? Here the same hybrid, in the same fields, is grown with no
nitrogen, 60, 120 and 180 kg per hectare, in each of 33 long-rains seasons.

```{ojs}
md`Averaged over the 33 seasons, the model's maize yields **${fmt.int(resp[0].mean)} kg/ha** without nitrogen and
**${fmt.int(resp[1].mean)}**, **${fmt.int(resp[2].mean)}** and **${fmt.int(resp[3].mean)} kg/ha** with 60, 120 and 180 kg
(dry matter). Each of the first 60 kg adds **${fmt.d1(aeModel)} kg** of grain. The response does not flatten
within the range tested. FAOSTAT puts Kenya's national maize yield at 1.56-1.77 t/ha in 2018-2020
(<a href="#ref-faostat_qcl">FAO 2025</a>): the model's crop without any fertiliser already out-yields the country's average field.`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 320, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Nitrogen applied (kg N/ha)", ticks: RATES},
  y: {label: "Grain yield, kg/ha (area-weighted, dry matter)", grid: true, domain: [0, 13000]},
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY(resp, {x: "n", y1: "p10", y2: "p90", fill: "#2b6cb0", fillOpacity: 0.15}),
    Plot.rectY([{y1: 1560, y2: 1774}], {x1: 0, x2: 180, y1: "y1", y2: "y2", fill: "#c98b2b", fillOpacity: 0.35}),
    Plot.text([{x: 178, y: 1774}], {x: "x", y: "y", text: () => "FAOSTAT Kenya, 2018-2020", textAnchor: "end", dy: -8, fill: "#8a5a12"}),
    Plot.line(resp, {x: "n", y: "mean", stroke: "#2b6cb0", strokeWidth: 2.5}),
    Plot.dot(resp, {x: "n", y: "mean", fill: "#2b6cb0", r: 5, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.n} kg N/ha\nmean ${fmt.int(d.mean)} kg/ha\nmedian ${fmt.int(d.p50)}\n10th-90th percentile ${fmt.int(d.p10)}-${fmt.int(d.p90)}`}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), "kenya_n_response", "line: mean of 33 seasons; band: 10th-90th percentile; brown: FAOSTAT national yield")
```

## The model's answer: always

The value-cost ratio (VCR) divides the value of the extra grain by the cost of the fertiliser that grew it.
At 1 the bag pays for itself; 2, a 100% return, is the usual bar for fertiliser to be worth buying, and 4 is
proposed where weather and prices are risky and farmers short of cash [@kiwia2022]. Set the two prices
below; the charts on the rest of the page follow them. The maize slider covers the range of the monthly
Eldoret wholesale price in 2021-2026.

```{ojs}
viewof maizePrice = Inputs.range([20, 95], {value: S.maize_price_ksh_kg.median, step: 0.5, label: "Maize price (KSh per kg of grain)"})
viewof nPrice = Inputs.radio(new Map([
  ["Subsidised bag, 2023: KSh 2,500 per 50 kg", S.n_price_ksh_kg_n["subsidised 2023"]],
  ["Subsidised urea, 2022: KSh 3,500 per 50 kg", S.n_price_ksh_kg_n["subsidised 2022"]],
  ["Market urea, 2022: KSh 6,500 per 50 kg", S.n_price_ksh_kg_n["market 2022"]]]),
  {value: S.n_price_ksh_kg_n["market 2022"], label: "Fertiliser price"})
viewof stepPick = Inputs.radio(new Map([["0 to 60 kg N", 0], ["60 to 120", 1], ["120 to 180", 2]]), {value: 0, label: "Step"})
```

```{ojs}
vcr = (row, a, b, s) => s * maizePrice * MARKET * (row.y[b] - row.y[a]) / (nPrice * (b - a))
vcrYears = byYear.map(r => {
  const [a, b] = STEPS[stepPick], v = vcr(r, a, b, share)
  return {year: r.year, vcr: v, gain: r.y[b] - r.y[a], cls: vcrClass(v)}
})
md`At **${fmt.d1(maizePrice)} KSh/kg** for maize and **${fmt.int(nPrice)} KSh** per kg of nitrogen, the step from
${stepName(stepPick)} has a median VCR of **${fmt.d1(d3.median(vcrYears, d => d.vcr))}**${share < 1 ?
` with the farm getting ${fmt.pct(share)} of the model's response` : ""}. It pays back in
**${fmt.pct(d3.mean(vcrYears, d => d.vcr >= 1))}** of the 33 seasons, doubles the money in
**${fmt.pct(d3.mean(vcrYears, d => d.vcr >= 2))}** and passes the risk-proof bar of 4 in
**${fmt.pct(d3.mean(vcrYears, d => d.vcr >= 4))}**.`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 300, marginLeft: 50,
  x: {label: null, type: "band", tickFormat: d => d % 5 === 0 ? String(d) : ""},
  y: {label: `Value-cost ratio, ${stepName(stepPick)}`, grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, ...vcrColor},
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(vcrYears, {x: "year", y: "vcr", fill: "cls", inset: 1, tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.year}\nextra grain ${fmt.int(d.gain)} kg/ha (dry)\nVCR ${fmt.d1(d.vcr)}`}),
    Plot.ruleY([1, 2, 4], {stroke: "#333", strokeDasharray: "3,3"}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}), "kenya_vcr_by_year", "one bar per long-rains season; dashed lines at VCR 1, 2 and 4")
```

## How wrong can the model be?

```{ojs}
md`Too good to be true? The model's field has no weeds, pests or diseases and never runs short of phosphorus
or potassium; its hybrid grows with DSSAT's standard coefficients. Farm fields are not like that. In 2009-2013 maize trials on farms in Kakamega, Busia and Embu counties, each of the first 60 kg of
nitrogen (given with 20-22 kg phosphorus) added about **${KIWIA_AEN} kg** of grain, a VCR of about 2, and the
fertilised plot yielded less than the unfertilised one in 24% of the trials (<a href="#ref-kiwia2022">Kiwia et al. 2022</a>). The model adds
**${fmt.d1(aeModel * MARKET)} kg** of grain at 14% moisture: the trial farms got about
**${fmt.pct(anchor)}** of the model's response (the trials do not state the grain moisture; on a dry basis the
share would be ${fmt.pct(KIWIA_AEN / aeModel)}).

So the model's kilograms are not to be trusted, but its answer can be tested for how much error it can
absorb. The slider below scales the model's response down to the share a real farm gets. Every chart on the
page follows it.`
```

```{ojs}
viewof share = Inputs.range([0.05, 1], {value: 1, step: 0.01, label: "Share of the model's response a farm gets"})
viewof thr = Inputs.radio(new Map([["1: costs back", 1], ["2: doubles the money", 2], ["4: safe under risk", 4]]),
  {value: 2, label: "A step pays when its VCR is at least"})
```

```{ojs}
curve = d3.range(0.05, 1.0001, 0.01).flatMap(s => STEPS.map(([a, b], k) => ({
  s, step: stepName(k), frac: d3.mean(byYear, r => vcr(r, a, b, s) >= thr)})))
half = STEPS.map(([a, b], k) => ({step: stepName(k), s50: thr / d3.median(byYear, r => vcr(r, a, b, 1))}))
md`With these prices, the first 60 kg still reach a VCR of ${thr} in half of the seasons as long as a farm gets at
least **${fmt.pct(half[0].s50)}** of the model's response${half[0].s50 > anchor ? ", **more than the trial farms got**" :
", less than the trial farms got"}. For the step from 120 to 180 kg the bar is **${fmt.pct(half[2].s50)}**.
${half.some(h => h.s50 > 1) ? "A share above 100% means the step does not reach the bar in half the seasons even at the model's full response." : ""}`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 320, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: "Share of the model's response a farm gets", tickFormat: "%", domain: [0, 1]},
  y: {label: `Share of seasons with VCR of at least ${thr}`, tickFormat: "%", domain: [0, 1], grid: true},
  color: {legend: true, domain: STEPS.map((_, k) => stepName(k)), range: ["#1f5f99", "#4f9a6a", "#c98b2b"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleX([anchor], {stroke: "#888", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.text([anchor], {x: d => d, y: 1, text: () => "Kenya trials", textAnchor: "start", dx: 4, dy: 6, fill: "#666"}),
    Plot.ruleX([share], {stroke: "#d0021b"}),
    Plot.line(curve, {x: "s", y: "frac", stroke: "step", strokeWidth: 2}),
    Plot.tip(curve, Plot.pointerX({x: "s", y: "frac",
      title: d => `${d.step}\nfarm gets ${fmt.pct(d.s)} of the model's response\nVCR >= ${thr} in ${fmt.pct(d.frac)} of seasons`}))
  ]
}), "kenya_breakeven_share", "red: the share chosen above; dashed: on-farm trials in Kenya (Kiwia et al. 2022)")
```

## The price of a sack

The weather is not the only risk. The same bag bought at planting is repaid by grain sold months later, at
whatever price the market then pays.

```{ojs}
pMin = price.reduce((a, b) => (b.ksh_kg < a.ksh_kg ? b : a))
pMax = price.reduce((a, b) => (b.ksh_kg > a.ksh_kg ? b : a))
md`Eldoret's wholesale maize price ranged from **${fmt.d1(pMin.ksh_kg)} KSh/kg** (${pMin.date.toISOString().slice(0, 7)}) to
**${fmt.d1(pMax.ksh_kg)} KSh/kg** (${pMax.date.toISOString().slice(0, 7)}) in the ${price.length} months on record.`
```

```{ojs}
priceBar = {
  const [a, b] = STEPS[stepPick]
  const gain = d3.median(byYear, r => r.y[b] - r.y[a])
  return thr * nPrice * (b - a) / (share * MARKET * gain)
}
below = price.filter(d => d.ksh_kg < priceBar).length
md`For the step from ${stepName(stepPick)}, with the farm getting ${fmt.pct(share)} of the model's response, a
median season reaches a VCR of ${thr} only when maize sells above **${fmt.d1(priceBar)} KSh/kg**. Eldoret's
wholesale price was below that in **${below} of ${price.length}** months.`
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 280, marginLeft: 60,
  x: {label: null, type: "utc"},
  y: {label: "Maize, wholesale, Eldoret (KSh/kg)", grid: true, domain: [0, Math.max(d3.max(price, d => d.ksh_kg) * 1.08, priceBar * 1.1)]},
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY([{x: d3.min(price, d => d.date)}, {x: d3.max(price, d => d.date)}],
      {x: "x", y1: 0, y2: priceBar, fill: "#c0392b", fillOpacity: 0.08}),
    Plot.ruleY([priceBar], {stroke: "#c0392b", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.ruleY([maizePrice], {stroke: "#2b6cb0"}),
    Plot.line(price, {x: "date", y: "ksh_kg", stroke: "#333", strokeWidth: 1.5}),
    Plot.dot(price, {x: "date", y: "ksh_kg", r: 2.5, fill: d => d.ksh_kg < priceBar ? "#c0392b" : "#333", tip: true,
      title: d => `${d.date.toISOString().slice(0, 7)}\n${fmt.d1(d.ksh_kg)} KSh/kg\n${d.ksh_kg < priceBar ? "below" : "above"} the price for VCR ${thr}`})
  ]
}), "kenya_maize_price", "WFP monthly wholesale price, white maize, 90 kg bags; red: below the price at which the step reaches the chosen VCR; blue: price chosen above")
```

## How far to go, cell by cell

```{ojs}
cellsK = cells.filter(d => d["180"] > 0).map(d => {
  const m = RATES.map(n => share * maizePrice * MARKET * (d[String(n)] - d["0"]) - nPrice * n)
  return {...d, best: RATES[m.indexOf(d3.max(m))], y0: d["0"], first: d["60"] - d["0"], gain: d3.max(m)}
})
bestHa = d3.rollups(cellsK, v => d3.sum(v, d => d.ha), d => d.best)
totalHa = d3.sum(cellsK, d => d.ha)
md`For each weather cell, the rate with the highest mean margin (the grain value it adds minus the fertiliser
cost) at the prices and share chosen above:
${RATES.map(n => { const h = (bestHa.find(e => e[0] === n) || [n, 0])[1]; return `**${n} kg N** on ${fmt.pct(h / totalHa)} of the maize area` }).join(", ")}.`
```

```{ojs}
viewof mapMetric = Inputs.radio(new Map([["Best N rate", "best"], ["Yield without N", "y0"], ["Grain from the first 60 kg", "first"]]),
  {value: "best", label: "Map"})
```

```{ojs}
withDownload(Plot.plot({
  height: 460, aspectRatio: 1,
  projection: {type: "equirectangular", domain: cellFeatures(cellsK)},
  color: mapMetric === "best"
    ? {type: "ordinal", domain: RATES, range: ["#f1e3c6", "#9ecae1", "#4292c6", "#08306b"], legend: true, label: "Best N rate (kg N/ha)"}
    : {scheme: "YlGnBu", legend: true, label: mapMetric === "y0" ? "Mean yield without N (kg/ha, dry)" : "Grain from the first 60 kg N (kg/ha, dry)"},
  marks: [
    Plot.geo(cellFeatures(cellsK), {fill: d => d.properties[mapMetric], stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.4}),
    ...placeMarks(Plot, adm1, adm2, {labels: "adm1", fontSize: 9}),
    Plot.tip(cellsK, Plot.pointer({x: "lon", y: "lat",
      title: d => `${d.lat.toFixed(2)} N, ${d.lon.toFixed(2)} E\nbest rate ${d.best} kg N/ha\nyield: ` +
        RATES.map(n => `${n} N ${fmt.int(d[String(n)])}`).join(", ") + ` kg/ha\nmaize ${fmt.int(d.ha)} ha`})),
    Plot.frame()
  ]
}), "kenya_cell_map", "0.1° AgERA5 cells with maize in MapSPAM 2020; mean of 33 seasons")
```

## What this does not say

- **Simulated, not observed.** Why the simulated yields differ from official statistics, in every case study:
  [FAQ](../about/faq.qmd#why-do-the-simulated-yields-differ-from-the-official-statistics).
- **Uncalibrated.** H610 runs with DSSAT's own coefficients, in a field without weeds, pests, diseases or
  phosphorus shortage. Its kilograms are not a forecast of farm yields; the share slider is there for
  that reason.
- **A rich soil.** Without fertiliser the model's crop still takes up about 100 kg N/ha a season from the
  soil, mineralised from the SoilGrids organic matter. A poorer soil would make nitrogen worth more, a
  richer one less.
- **Only the bag.** The VCR counts the fertiliser price alone: no transport, labour, credit or the cost of
  phosphorus that farmers usually buy with it. The 2023 subsidised price was reported without the type of
  fertiliser and is priced here as urea.
- **Prices from 2021-2026, weather from 1991-2023.** Every season is valued at the 2021-2026 price range, and one
  market stands for the whole box.
- **One sowing date.** Every season is sown on 15 March. A late start of the rains is a different
  experiment (see [Niger - Millet](niger.qmd)).

## Run it yourself

```bash
python scripts/prepare_weather.py   --config configs/cases/kenya-maize.yml
python scripts/prepare_crop_mask.py --config configs/cases/kenya-maize.yml
python scripts/prepare_soils.py     --config configs/cases/kenya-maize.yml --aoi kenya_maize
python scripts/run_aoi.py           --config configs/cases/kenya-maize.yml
python docs/scripts/export_cases.py kenya --wfp <folder>/wfp_food_prices_ken.csv
```

The export reads WFP's Kenya price file, downloaded from the Humanitarian Data Exchange
([`wfp_food_prices_ken.csv`](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/wfp-food-prices-for-kenya), CC BY-IGO). The three-year version of this
area ships with xdssat: `example-inputs/kenya_maize/` ([Examples](../xdssat/examples.qmd)).
